job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: In a Class 7 mathematics lesson, Mr. Sharma explained how integers work beyond simple counting. 'Think of a thermometer,' he said. 'If the temperature drops from 5 degrees to -5 degrees, the negative sign shows a value below zero, not just an instruction to subtract.' Rohan asked, 'But sir, isn't -10 smaller than -5 because 10 is bigger than 5?' Mr. Sharma smiled and drew a number line. 'On the number line, numbers to the left are always smaller. Since -10 is further left than -5, -10 is actually the smaller value.' Meera then asked about operations. 'If I have 8 and subtract -3, do I just get 5?' Mr. Sharma shook his head. 'Subtracting a negative is like adding a positive, so 8 minus -3 becomes 8 plus 3, which is 11. Also, remember that when multiplying two negative numbers, the result is always positive, like -4 times -3 equals 12.' Meera nodded, 'So, negative numbers are just as real as positive ones, representing things like debts or depths below sea level.' Mr. Sharma agreed, noting that these rules help us navigate real-world problems accurately without confusion.
